edges.claim: Body mediates sensory encounter; soul personalizes its impressions.
Spirit is distinguished from the soul's individual reactions.
The etheric principle is invoked in Steiner's account of plant life.
Steiner describes thought permeating sentient life as intellectual soul.
The intellectual soul is described as opening toward spiritual intuition.
Consciousness soul and spirit-self form a unity in the earthly person.
The ninefold arrangement becomes sevenfold through specified unions.
The fourfold account groups the soul body and sentient soul in astral body.
Spirit-self is described as transformation of astral body.
Life-spirit is described as transformation of life body.
Spirit-man is described as transformation of physical body.
Old Saturn is presented as the beginning of the human physical body's development.
Old Sun introduces the etheric/life body into the human constitution.
Old Moon is connected with reception of the astral body.
Earth is the evolutionary stage in which the I becomes active.

edges.claim: Steiner assigns an outpouring of will to the Thrones at Saturn's beginning.
Spirits of Wisdom are associated with the bestowal of the life body on Old Sun.
Archangels are connected with early sense-organ development on Saturn.
Saturn precedes Sun in Steiner's cosmic narrative.
Sun precedes Moon in Steiner's cosmic narrative.
Moon precedes Earth in Steiner's cosmic narrative.
Earth evolution initially recapitulates earlier developmental stages.
Each worldview orientation may be adopted with different soul moods.
Worldview combinations can receive an additional tonal qualification.
The twelve orientations are related symbolically to zodiacal signs.
The seven moods are related to planetary imagery within the zodiac.
The three tones are compared respectively with Sun, Moon and Earth.
Anthropomorphism is presented separately from the three primary tones.
Thinking-cognition is associated with waking consciousness.
Feeling is associated with dreaming consciousness.
Willing is associated with sleeping consciousness.
Head, chest/trunk and limbs form a distinct educational account of human organization.
Twelve sense regions are described as permeated by seven life processes.
Steiner likens sense regions to a human zodiac.
edges.note: An attributed analogy, not established neuroscience.
